description: Fix schedule calendar not rendering — add missing backend execution endpoints and execution tracking model

userStories.title: Create ScheduleExecution SQLAlchemy model and Pydantic schema
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a database model and schema for schedule execution records so the API can persist and return execution history.
acceptanceCriteria: Create SQLAlchemy model ScheduleExecution in backend/src/models/ with columns: id (UUID, PK), schedule_id (String, not null), thread_id (String, nullable), status (String, not null, default 'scheduled' — one of 'scheduled','running','success','failure'), scheduled_time (DateTime, not null), started_at (DateTime, nullable), completed_at (DateTime, nullable), error_message (Text, nullable), metadata (JSONB, default {}), user_id (String, not null)
Create Pydantic response schema ScheduleExecutionResponse in backend/src/schemas/entities/schedule.py matching the model fields
Table name should be 'schedule_executions'
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Follow existing SQLAlchemy model patterns in the codebase. The app uses PostgreSQL with async SQLAlchemy. Check backend/src/models/ or backend/src/services/db.py for DB connection patterns.

userStories.title: Create ScheduleExecutionService with CRUD operations
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a service layer to create, update, and query execution records from the database.
acceptanceCriteria: Create ScheduleExecutionService class in backend/src/services/schedule_execution.py
Implement create_execution(schedule_id, user_id, scheduled_time) -> ScheduleExecution
Implement update_execution(execution_id, status, thread_id=None, error_message=None, completed_at=None)
Implement get_recent_executions(user_id, limit=20) -> list ordered by scheduled_time desc
Implement get_executions_by_schedule(schedule_id, user_id) -> list ordered by scheduled_time desc
Implement get_executions_by_date_range(user_id, start, end) -> list filtered by scheduled_time
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use async SQLAlchemy patterns consistent with the existing codebase. Check backend/src/services/ for examples of how other services handle DB sessions.

userStories.title: Record execution lifecycle in scheduled_llm_invoke
userStories.description: As a system, I need to track each schedule execution from dispatch through completion so users can see run history.
acceptanceCriteria: In backend/src/services/schedule.py scheduled_llm_invoke function, insert a schedule_execution row with status 'running' and started_at=now when execution begins
On successful completion, update status to 'success', set completed_at and thread_id
On failure/exception, update status to 'failure', set completed_at and error_message
Both distributed mode (TaskIQ dispatch) and in-process mode paths are covered
Existing schedule create/update/delete functionality is not broken
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The scheduled_llm_invoke function in backend/src/services/schedule.py has two code paths: distributed (DISTRIBUTED_WORKERS=True dispatches via run_agent_stream.kiq()) and in-process (direct agent.invoke). Both need execution tracking. user_id and title are already available as function parameters.

userStories.title: Add GET /schedules/executions/recent endpoint
userStories.description: As a frontend consumer, I need an endpoint to fetch recent executions across all schedules so the calendar and sidebar can display them.
acceptanceCriteria: Add GET /schedules/executions/recent route to backend/src/routes/v0/schedule.py
CRITICAL: This route MUST be defined BEFORE the GET /schedules/{job_id} route to avoid 'executions' being captured as a job_id path parameter
Accepts optional query parameter limit (int, default 20)
Returns JSON array of ScheduleExecutionResponse objects
Results ordered by scheduled_time descending
Scoped to authenticated user's schedules only (use ProtectedUser dependency)
Returns [] empty array when no executions exist
Returns content-type: application/json (not text/html)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Route ordering is critical in FastAPI. The /executions/recent path must come before /{job_id} or FastAPI will try to match 'executions' as a job_id. Check existing routes in backend/src/routes/v0/schedule.py for auth patterns.

userStories.title: Add GET /schedules/{schedule_id}/executions endpoint
userStories.description: As a frontend consumer, I need to fetch executions for a specific schedule.
acceptanceCriteria: Add GET /schedules/{schedule_id}/executions route to backend/src/routes/v0/schedule.py
Returns JSON array of ScheduleExecutionResponse objects ordered by scheduled_time desc
Returns 404 if schedule doesn't exist or doesn't belong to user
Requires authentication via ProtectedUser
Returns content-type: application/json
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This route uses a path parameter for the schedule ID. It should be placed after the /executions/recent and /executions routes but can go before or after /{job_id} since it has a longer path prefix.

userStories.title: Add GET /schedules/executions endpoint with date range filtering
userStories.description: As a frontend consumer, I need to fetch executions within a date range so the calendar can display events for the visible window.
acceptanceCriteria: Add GET /schedules/executions route to backend/src/routes/v0/schedule.py
CRITICAL: This route MUST be defined BEFORE the GET /schedules/{job_id} route
Accepts optional query parameters start (ISO datetime) and end (ISO datetime)
Defaults to last 30 days if start/end not provided
Returns JSON array of ScheduleExecutionResponse objects
Scoped to authenticated user's schedules only
Returns content-type: application/json
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Place this route alongside the /executions/recent route, before /{job_id}. The frontend calls this as /api/schedules/executions?start=<ISO>&end=<ISO>.

userStories.title: Generate projected future executions from cron expressions
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see upcoming scheduled runs on the calendar so I can visualize when my agents will execute next.
acceptanceCriteria: Add croniter to backend dependencies in pyproject.toml (if not already present)
Create a utility function that takes a cron expression and returns projected execution times for the next 30 days
The /executions/recent and /executions (date range) endpoints include projected future executions with status 'scheduled'
Projected executions have no started_at or completed_at values
Projected executions use synthetic IDs in format '{schedule_id}_proj_{iso_time}' to avoid collisions with real records
Projected executions include the schedule_id and user_id from the parent schedule
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use croniter library to compute next N occurrences from a cron expression. Each schedule's trigger.expression contains the cron string. The frontend getCalendarDateRange covers 30 days past and 30 days future, so project up to 30 days ahead.
